tiers.name: Four rooms and a porridge pan
Dining room with a proper stove
A guest lounge with a telescope

events.line: A cycling tour has taken the whole top floor and left a very good review.
The midges were out in force. Guests spent breakfast indoors and checked out a day early.
The ferry ran late, and a boatload of stranded travellers found your sign.
A gale took out the power and the road. Not one guest arrived, and the candles went in the porridge.
A party of New Year visitors has booked out the house and brought a fiddle.
Landscape photographers asked for breakfast at four in the morning. They paid well for the privilege.

upgrades.name: Rooms in the old stable block
upgrades.text: More beds and more breakfasts, and a longer list of things that can go wrong on a Sunday night.

upgrades.name: Evening meals with the local catch
upgrades.text: Visitors will pay for a proper dinner on an island. They will also tell you how it compares.

upgrades.name: A place in the island's visitor guide
upgrades.text: Your name where the ferry passengers look.

asks.title: The Highland Games weekend
asks.text: It is the weekend of the Skye Highland Games and every bed in Portree has been spoken for, twice. {deed} has had a dozen calls today.

options.label: Take every booking and put camp beds in the lounge
options.say: A house full of pipers, tossers of cabers and one very polite cyclist. The camp beds are a hit.

risk.say: Two double-bookings, a lost key and a pipe band in the hall at six. The reviews are mixed.

options.label: Take what the rooms hold and no more
options.say: Full, calm and everyone has a bed. A very ordinary triumph.

options.label: Leave the phone off the hook
options.say: The phone rings on without you. Someone else's guests get the shortbread.
